newsitem.title: FRANCE: French health spending rises slightly in February.
newsitem.headline: French health spending rises slightly in February.

text.p: French healthcare spending in February was a slight 0.1 percent higher at 36.13 billion francs compared with January when spending had been stable, national health insurance fund Caisse Nationale d'Assurance Maladie (CNAM) said on Saturday.

CNAM said that payments for private specialists -- dentists and independent doctors -- were 0.2 percent lower, but expenditure on prescriptions was 0.3 percent higher with an 0.7 percent increase for pharmacies.
Sickness pay was 0.4 percent higher, which CNAM said was the result of an influenza epidemic.
Hospitalisation costs were 0.1 percent higher, with stability in public hospitals and a one percent rise in private establishments.
CNAM said the cumulative 1997 health spending to end-February stood at 74.015 billion francs.

The index for the month, with January 1990 as base, stood at 133.9. The February figure was up 0.1 percent on January 1997 and the same percentage since the start of the year. It was 0.1 percent down on February 1996.
